Definition: middle voice from G3056; to take an inventory, i.e. estimate (literally or figuratively):--conclude, (ac-)count (of), + despise, esteem, impute, lay, number, reason, reckon, suppose, think (on).
BiblicalUsage: logízomai means to reckon, to count, to think, and it is one of those words that quietly holds a whole theme together. In Romans 4:3, "and it was counted unto him for righteousness."; and in 2 Corinthians 5:19, "not imputing their trespasses unto them". In 1 Corinthians 13:5, "thinketh no evil"; and in Romans 8:18, "For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time [are] not worthy [to be compared] with the glory which shall be revealed in us.".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe reckoning is the arithmetic of grace — Abraham believed, and it was counted to him for righteousness, and God does not impute our trespasses to us in Christ. I hold that love thinketh no evil, and the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come. My position is that I will let God do the counting: my sins reckoned to Christ, and His righteousness reckoned to me.
